Department: Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute

DescriptionOPEN DATE: September 11, 2026                    CLOSING DATE: October 12, 2026               POSITION TYPE: Trust FundAPPOINTMENT TYPE: Temporary for 2 years   SCHEDULE: Full Time
DUTY LOCATION: Washington, DC, National Museum of Natural History 



Position sensitivity and risk: 
Non-Sensitive - Low risk 

Who May Apply:
Open to all qualified applicants

What are Trust Fund Positions?
Trust Fund positions are unique to the Smithsonian. They are paid for from a variety of sources, including the Smithsonian endowment, revenue from our business activities, donations, grants and contracts. Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. The salary ranges for trust positions are generally the same as for federal positions and in many cases trust and federal employees work side by side. Trust employees have their own benefit program, which may include Health, Dental & Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Transit/Commuter Benefits, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, Annual and Sick Leave, Family Friendly Leave, 403b Retirement Plan, Discounts for Smithsonian Memberships, Museum Stores and Restaurants, Credit Union, Smithsonian Early Enrichment Center (Child Care), Flexible Spending Account (Health & Dependent Care). Conditions of Employment
Pass Pre-employment Background Check and Subsequent Background Investigation for position designated.
Complete a Probationary Period.
Maintain a Bank Account for Direct Deposit/Electronic Transfer.
The position is open to all candidates eligible to work in the United States.  Proof of eligibility to work in U.S. is not required to apply.
Applicants must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement. 

OVERVIEWThis position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).


STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests. 

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIESData Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)
Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.
Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.
Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.
Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.
Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.
Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.
Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.
Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.
Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.
Uses programming languages and tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, GIS applications, and related scientific and data-management software.
Identifies data-quality problems, inconsistencies, missing values, formatting issues, and other anomalies and determines appropriate methods for correcting or documenting them.
Works with researchers and other technical personnel to ensure that processed data and analyticalproducts meet established scientific and program requirements.


Requirements Gathering and Technical Support (25%)

Works closely with researchers and program personnel to identify data-processing, analytical, software, and data-management requirements for assigned scientific projects.
Conducts technical analyses of available methods and alternatives and recommends appropriate software tools, workflows, calculations, and analytical approaches.
Assists researchers in translating scientific requirements into practical data-processing and
computational solutions.
Evaluates existing workflows and recommends modifications when established approaches do not fully address the characteristics of the data or requirements of an assigned project.
Coordinates with site representatives concerning timelines and technical requirements for acquisition and submission of plot inventory, TLS, ALS, GNSS, and related scientific data.
Reviews submitted data to determine whether established ForestGEO and GEO-TREES formatting, documentation, and data-quality requirements have been met.
Works with site personnel to resolve routine and moderately complex data-submission and data-quality problems.
Coordinates with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and other appropriate technical staff to ensure assigned development activities follow applicable systems-development, documentation, version-control, security, and software-development practices.
Prepares technical documentation describing data-processing workflows, code, data structures, analytical procedures, and related methods.
Assists in testing new or modified software tools, workflows, and procedures prior to implementation.


Training and Collaboration (25%)

Develops and provides formal and informal training to researchers, site personnel, and program partners concerning ForestGEO and GEO-TREES data systems, data-management procedures, formatting requirements, data-processing workflows, and related tools.
Serves as a technical point of contact for tree-inventory teams and other users at assigned ForestGEO and GEO-TREES sites.
Provides advice, training, troubleshooting assistance, and technical support concerning data collection, formatting, cleaning, validation, processing, documentation, and submission.
Explains data standards, analytical procedures, software requirements, and data-management practices to researchers and partners with varying levels of technical expertise.
Collaborates with scientists, data managers, programmers, and other personnel to identify and resolve data-management and processing problems.
Participates in meetings, working groups, and collaborative activities involving ForestGEO, GEO-TREES, Smithsonian staff, and domestic and international research partners.
Shares information concerning lessons learned, recurring data problems, workflow improvements, and effective data-management practices with program staff and partners.

jobs_results.description: Created in our Life Science Transformation Office (now part of the Technology Office) and still transformational at heart, the Digital Center of Excellence team (DiCE) is an agile and forward-thinking team of currently 70 + highly motivated individuals that thrives on facilitating, streamlining, and accelerating the conception, development and scaling of high-quality digital solutions that solve our Life Science customers’ challenges. We value teamwork, innovation, and a passion for learning. As part of DiCE R&D enablement, you will work on accelerating early phases of scientific software development, and on crafting scientific algorithms for groundbreaking, digital platforms. You will use your knowledge and understanding of AI, cheminformatics, and bioinformatics tools to develop digital tools that answer the toughest challenges in Life Science. Your strong interpersonal skills and knowledge of computational techniques in biology and chemistry enable you to make strides at the forefront of digital innovation. You will be working in an interdisciplinary team that includes lab managers, chemists, biologists, data scientists, and software engineers based around the world. Main responsibilities: In this role, you need to understand and translate R&D lab needs into product requirements for prototype construction, scientific algorithm development, and final product development by software engineering teams. You will be typically involved in activities, such as: Analyzing complex problems in Life Science and articulating solution ideas based on ChemInformatics, BioInformatics and AI/ML approaches Providing proof-of-concepts for testing out R&D lab ideas Following an agile development approach in building PoC and core software modules. You will contribute to the development of the scientific component of the software and work in close collaboration with cross functional software engineering teams e.g. UI/UX experts Keeping up with the latest development in computational chemistry, computational biology and machine-driven drug discovery in publications to improve the existing digital products based on them Building the computational chemistry engine for drug discovery or lab automation purpose based on ML/AL and other procedural algorithms. Curating large datasets and building predictive models from them Applying ML/AL on the traditional computational science approaches Documenting data, data curation and model building processes Who youa are Minimum Qualifications: Masters or PhD degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Cheminformatics, Chemical Engineering, Computer Science or related fields. Minimum of 5 years industry experience. Experience working in multi-disciplinary and cross-culture teams Excellent communication skills Be curious and innovative with a strong desire to revolutionize the life science industry What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We celebrate all dimensions of diversity and believe that it drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. (ID: 2026-3884)




    Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in                translational research, biomedical informatics, and data                science applications to research centers and healthcare                organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in                biomedical science, software engineering, and program                management, we focus on developing and applying research                tools and techniques to empower decision-making and                accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the                top research organizations and facilities in the country                including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of                Health (NIH).


    Benefits We Offer:

            100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees        Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays        401K match up to 5%        Educational Benefits for Career Growth        Employee Referral Bonus                    Flexible Spending Accounts:                            Healthcare (FSA)                Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK)                Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP)                Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN)                        Position Overview

 

The Bioinformatics Scientist will address the bioinformatics, scientific computing, and data analysis needs of investigators within the NIAID Division of Intramural Research (DIR) and their collaborators, as part of the Integrated Data Sciences Section (IDSS) within the Research Technologies Branch (RTB), with particular emphasis on HIV research. The incumbent will provide analysis support across genomic and clinical research data — including viral sequence, host–pathogen, and immunologic datasets generated by HIV studies — develop and maintain production pipelines, and contribute to a scalable resource supporting NIAID scientists. A substantial portion of the work will directly support HIV investigators and their laboratory and clinical research teams. The successful candidate will be highly motivated, adaptable, structured, and detail-oriented.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Scientific consultation. Address the bioinformatics, scientific computing, and data analysis needs of users within the NIAID Division of Intramural Research and their collaborators, providing expertise in the statistical design of biological experiments involving high-throughput genome-scale technologies, data mining and knowledge discovery techniques, automated workflow development, and experimental design consultation.

Bioinformatics support. Provide support spanning somatic and germline variant calling and analysis, single-cell and bulk gene expression analysis, de novo assembly of genomes and transcriptomes, comparative genomics of model and non-model organisms, proteomics, ChIP-seq, and ATAC-seq, including development of high-throughput pipelines for these data modalities.

Programming support. Provide programming and troubleshooting support to the Research Technologies Branch and collaborating Institutes in the dissemination of research data.

Data analysis. Perform computational data analysis on genomic and clinical research data, and provide statistical support and analysis on research data.

Collaboration. Work with staff on scientific programming and experimental design.

Publication. Contribute to and co-author scientific publications in leading peer-reviewed journals.

Resource development. Contribute to the development of a scalable and flexible resource providing next-generation sequencing bioinformatics, structural and computational biology, and machine learning data support to NIAID scientists and investigators.

 

The Bioinformatics Scientist is expected to bring strong skills in the following areas:

Next-generation sequencing analysis (whole-exome, whole-genome, RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, using both long- and short-read technologies)

Statistical modeling

Scripting

Biological interpretation

 

Required Qualifications

 

Clearance. Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust security clearance.

Education. Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in a related field; master’s degree or doctorate preferred.

Experience. Four or more years of experience in bioinformatics, including two or more years developing and maintaining production bioinformatics pipelines.

Programming languages. Expert-level proficiency in two of the following: Python, R, C/C++, sh/bash.

Containerization. Experience building images using one of the following: Docker, Podman, Singularity/Apptainer.

Pipeline frameworks. Expert-level proficiency in one pipeline framework: Snakemake, Nextflow, or CWL/WDL.

Documentation. Demonstrated expertise building technical and user documentation for tools, pipelines, and applications.

Infrastructure. Experience building pipelines on-premises using available high-performance computing infrastructure.

 

Preferred Qualifications

 

Experience supporting HIV research, including the analysis of HIV sequence data — for example viral genome assembly, phylogenetic and quasi-species analysis, drug-resistance profiling, or characterization of the latent reservoir.

Familiarity with HIV and infectious disease data resources and host–pathogen study designs, including integration of viral sequence data with host genomic, transcriptomic, or immunologic datasets.

Experience building pipelines or applications in the cloud using AWS, GCP, or Azure.

Experience building applications using one of the following frameworks: Django, Flask, RShiny, Electron, Flutter, or React.

Experience working in a laboratory setting.

Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH).
